THE FACTS BEHIND THE EXTENSION

About Twinprice

Twinprice is a free, open-source currency converter extension for Chrome and Firefox, published under the name Krlo. It helps you compare foreign prices while browsing by showing converted amounts beside the originals or in their place.

Product information checked 14 September 2026.

Twinprice at a glance

What Twinprice supports
ProductA browser extension for converting supported prices on ordinary webpages.
BrowsersGoogle Chrome and Mozilla Firefox. Check each official store listing for current compatibility and release details.
Price and accountFree to install and use. No Twinprice account required.
Conversion optionsConvert a page, one highlighted price, or an amount entered in the popup.
CurrenciesManual selection uses Frankfurter’s active currency catalog. AUTO detection uses a smaller curated set. Available pairs depend on the provider.
Display and undoKeep both prices or replace the original; customize converted-price colors and shape. Restore original prices from the popup.
Automatic conversionOptional for sites you choose, with a remembered source currency or AUTO mode.
LimitsPrices in images and inaccessible frames cannot be converted. Browser settings pages and extension stores restrict access. Some page layouts or ambiguous symbols need a manual source currency.
PaymentConversion changes the price displayed in your browser. It does not change the shop’s charge, process payments, or exchange money.

Follow the illustrated user guide or explore practical shopping examples.

Who publishes and maintains Twinprice?

Both the Chrome Web Store listing and the Firefox Add-ons listing identify the publisher as Krlo. Those are the official installation links for Twinprice.

The project’s source code and maintenance history are public in somewordshere/CurrencyConversionAddon on GitHub. You can inspect the implementation, follow changes, or report a reproducible problem there.

Twinprice is distributed under the MIT license. See the changelog and release files for its development history. Browser-store releases can become available at different times; use your store listing for the version currently offered to you.

Where do Twinprice’s exchange rates come from?

Twinprice retrieves reference exchange rates from Frankfurter and performs the conversion inside your browser. Frankfurter documents its currency coverage and underlying official data sources on its website.

Converted amounts help compare prices. They do not include payment-provider margins, card fees, shipping, or taxes that are not part of the displayed amount. The reference rate can differ from the rate used when you pay. See the guide’s checkout example.

Recent cached rates may be used while fresh ones are unavailable. Twinprice warns after 48 hours and will not use cached rates older than seven days. The website demo and guide examples use illustrative rates rather than a live quote.

What does Twinprice read or send?

Price detection and webpage changes run locally in the browser. Page contents, selected price values, visited URLs, and browsing history are not sent to the developer or the exchange-rate provider. Exchange-rate requests include currency codes; as with normal internet requests, the provider’s infrastructure may receive network details such as an IP address.

Webpage access lets Twinprice detect and convert supported prices. Storage permissions keep preferences and cached rates, and the context-menu permission provides the right-click conversion action. The extension does not add advertising or analytics trackers.

Read the full privacy policy for browser-specific storage, permissions, and rate-request details. You can turn off scanning, prompts, and automatic conversion by disabling Enable converter in the popup.

Help improve Twinprice

For bugs or feature requests, use the project’s issue tracker. Include your browser, extension version, and steps to reproduce the problem; leave out personal shopping or payment details.

If you have used Twinprice, you can share an honest review on its Chrome listing or Firefox listing. Describe what worked for you and what could be improved.
